sourcedFrom: PATRIOT™ BOLT ACTION CENTERFIRE RIFLE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 102353, typeset 2/15/18 (2018 (typesetting stamp 2/15/18 on every page; no separate copyright line is printed))
cleanIntro: A Patriot cleans as a bolt gun should: magazine out, bolt out, and then the two things that actually matter — a bore cleaned from the breech end where you can reach it, and bolt-to-receiver surfaces free of solid residue, which is what causes a bolt not to close and a round not to fire.

steps.title: Safety fully rearward before anything else moves
steps.action: Pull the safety lever on the right of the receiver fully rearward to ON. On a Patriot the bolt still operates with the safety either way, so the safety being on is not evidence the rifle is empty — it is just the first of the things you do in order.
steps.quote: Pull the safety lever fully rearward to the “ON” (SAFE) position (Fig. 1).
steps.cite: PATRIOT™ BOLT ACTION CENTERFIRE RIFLE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 102353, typeset 2/15/18 — REMOVING THE BOLT FROM THE FIREARM, p.16

steps.title: Magazine out — and it does not unload the rifle
steps.action: On removable-magazine models pull the magazine release latch rearward and let the magazine drop into your hand; fixed-magazine models unload through the action instead. Either way the chamber may still hold a round, and Mossberg prints that warning in capitals for a reason — a rifle with the magazine out will still fire.
steps.aside: Removal of the magazine will not unload the firearm!
steps.quote: Remove the magazine by pulling the magazine release latch rearward (Fig. 10).
steps.cite: PATRIOT™ BOLT ACTION CENTERFIRE RIFLE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 102353, typeset 2/15/18 — REMOVING THE MAGAZINE, p.9

steps.title: Open it and prove the chamber empty by eye and by finger
steps.action: Lift the bolt handle, draw the bolt back and look into the chamber and the receiver, then put a finger in. A brass case in a shadowed receiver is easy to miss and impossible to miss by touch. Keep the muzzle pointed somewhere that would not matter throughout.
steps.quote: Raise the bolt handle and pull the bolt part way to the rear of the action.
steps.cite: PATRIOT™ BOLT ACTION CENTERFIRE RIFLE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 102353, typeset 2/15/18 — REMOVING THE BOLT FROM THE FIREARM, p.16

steps.title: Bolt stop pressed, bolt out the back
steps.action: With the bolt partway back, press the bolt stop at the left rear of the receiver and draw the bolt straight out. It is the only thing holding the bolt in — people pull harder instead of pressing it and conclude the rifle does not come apart.
steps.quote: Depress the bolt stop at the left rear of the receiver to withdraw the bolt rearward out of the receiver (Fig. 15).
steps.cite: PATRIOT™ BOLT ACTION CENTERFIRE RIFLE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 102353, typeset 2/15/18 — REMOVING THE BOLT FROM THE FIREARM, p.16

steps.title: That is the strip — and it is where Mossberg stops
steps.action: Bolt out is the whole of the owner's teardown, with the barrelled action coming out of the stock as the only other permitted separation. The bolt does not come apart: the shroud, striker and spring are under compression and Mossberg routes that to a certified gunsmith.
steps.quote: The bolt can be removed from the barreled action, and the barreled action can
steps.cite: PATRIOT™ BOLT ACTION CENTERFIRE RIFLE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 102353, typeset 2/15/18 — THE BOLT ASSEMBLY AND RECEIVER, p.17

steps.title: Glasses on, then the bolt and its sliding surfaces
steps.action: Wear eye protection for the cleaning too — solvent flicks off a brush more than people expect. Give the bolt's sliding surfaces and the receiver's raceways real attention: solid residue there is what stops a bolt closing fully, and a bolt that is not fully closed is a misfire waiting to be blamed on ammunition.
steps.aside: In the receiver, special attention should be given to the bolt sliding surfaces.
steps.quote: Always wear eye protection during cleaning and lubrication.
steps.cite: PATRIOT™ BOLT ACTION CENTERFIRE RIFLE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 102353, typeset 2/15/18 — CLEANING AND LUBRICATION, p.16

steps.title: Bore from the breech end where you can
steps.action: Clean from breech to muzzle whenever the setup allows, which on a bolt gun it does — the bolt is out and the chamber is open. If you must go in from the muzzle, guide the rod carefully: the crown is the last quarter inch of rifling and a rod rubbing it costs accuracy that no amount of cleaning gets back.
steps.quote: Whenever possible, use cleaning products that allow cleaning the bore from breech to muzzle.
steps.cite: PATRIOT™ BOLT ACTION CENTERFIRE RIFLE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 102353, typeset 2/15/18 — THE BARREL, p.17

steps.title: Brush, patch, repeat, then a light oiled patch
steps.action: Brass brush with solvent through the bore several times, then dry patches one after another until they come out with nothing on them. Finish with one lightly oiled patch — a film, not a coat. Over-oiling a bore just collects the next lot of fouling and prints the first shot somewhere unexpected.
steps.aside: Do not over-lubricate, a light film is recommended.
steps.quote: Using a brass cleaning brush moistened with solvent, scrub the bore several times.
steps.cite: PATRIOT™ BOLT ACTION CENTERFIRE RIFLE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 102353, typeset 2/15/18 — THE BARREL, p.17

steps.title: Inspect while it is apart, and check the brake if fitted
steps.action: Look for cracks, chips or unusual wear while everything is open, and stop if you find any. If the rifle wears a muzzle brake, check it is still tight on the barrel — Mossberg asks for that periodically, and a brake backing off changes point of impact before it comes off entirely.
steps.quote: PERIODICALLY CHECK THAT THE MUZZLE BRAKE (IF SO EQUIPPED) IS TIGHTENED FIRMLY ONTO THE BARREL.
steps.cite: PATRIOT™ BOLT ACTION CENTERFIRE RIFLE — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 102353, typeset 2/15/18 — FUNCTION TESTING, p.18

deepAbsentReason: Mossberg publishes no deeper procedure for an owner. The manual's own line is that the bolt can come out of the barreled action and the barreled action out of the stock, "but further disassembly should be performed by a certified gunsmith only" — which rules out the bolt's own internals, the trigger and the bottom metal. There is nothing past the field strip to author, so the absence is recorded rather than filled with a procedure from somewhere else.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Brass brush and solvent, breech to muzzle where possible
Dry patches until they come out clean, then one lightly oiled patch
Protect the crown if you must clean from the muzzle

cleaning.name: BOLT & RECEIVER
tasks: Clean the bolt's sliding surfaces and the receiver raceways free of solid residue
Solid residue here stops the bolt closing properly and causes misfires
Light oil on external metal to prevent rust; do not flood it

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE & FEED
tasks: Wipe the magazine body and follower; no oil inside where it meets ammunition
Check the feed area is free of grit before the bolt goes back

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Wipe barrel and metalwork with a lightly oiled cloth after handling
Camouflage finishes: keep strong solvents and insect repellent off them

reassembly: Bolt handle up and to the right, locking lugs lined up with the machined cuts in the rear of the receiver.
⛔ Check the bolt sleeve orientation first: with the handle up and right, the tab on the sleeve must be horizontal and to the LEFT. Wrong, and the bolt will not close and the tab hits the stock.
Push the bolt forward about an inch until the bolt stop snaps in behind the lugs.
Bolt fully forward, handle rotated clockwise and down to closed.
Read the cocking indicator at the rear of the bolt — flush with the sleeve ring means cocked.
Magazine back in (removable-magazine models), then function test before any live ammunition.
fncheck: With the rifle empty and pointed somewhere safe, work the bolt several times — the bolt stop should keep it from coming out on its own. On a Lightning Bolt Action trigger, press the blade until your finger meets the trigger and let it return slowly; it should come back on its own every time. Then close the action with the safety ON and pull the trigger: the firing pin must not release. Finger off, safety to OFF: it must still not release. Safety OFF and trigger pulled: it should. Anything else and it goes to the Product Service Center.
